text.p: The confrontation in the United States between tobacco manufacturers and those seeking compensation for allegedly tobacco related illnesses is hotting up.
The question that Proteus readers want answered is whether insurers will be spectators or participants in this multi-billion dollar contest.
As with anything involving the U.S. legal system, we will all have to wait a long time for that answer and it probably won't be a simple one.
The tobacco firms are seeking to keep their insurers out of the fray. The reasons for this tactic were outlined in our piece (B.A.T plays down tobacco insurance cover) on Friday.

At least some of the State authorities backing the campaign for compensation aim to include insurers in the list of those contributing to any pay-out. They believe that they have a strong case and draw comparisons with pollution and the creation of Superfund.
Insurers and the tobacco lobby say the situation is quite different from the question of who should pay to clean up polluted industrial sites.

At the end of the day, whether insurers will be able to stay on the sidelines or not will be decided by lawyers wrangling over policy wordings dating back decades in some cases. The one certainty is that insurers will once again be running up large legal bills.
